title: Reporting, Fiori Analytics & Exam Revision
intro: The reports people actually use, what changed in S/4HANA, how to approach C_TS452, and how to package this course as a sellable training module.

lessons.title: Reports and Fiori analytics
lessons.body:
Purchasing reports

  • ME2M / ME2L / ME2N POs by material / supplier / number
  • ME80FN general purchasing analysis
  • ME5A requisitions; ME3L/ME3M outline agreements

Inventory reports

  • MMBE stock overview; MB52 warehouse stock; MB51 material documents
  • MB5B stock on posting date; MB5T stock in transit; ME2O subcontracting stock

Invoice reports

  • MIR5 invoice list; MB5S GR/IR balances; MRBR blocked invoices

Fiori analytical apps (names vary by release)

  • Procurement overview page: tiles/cards for spend, open POs, overdue items
  • Monitor Purchase Order Items, Purchase Order Average Delivery Time, Off-Contract Spend, Supplier Evaluation
  • Stock – Multiple Materials, Inventory KPI Analysis, Material Documents Overview

ALV tips for any classic report

  • Filter, sort, sum, subtotal; change layout and save layouts
  • Export to spreadsheet

Teaching end users to save their own ALV layout is a five-minute win they'll thank you for.
lessons.narration: Let's round up the reports people actually use. For purchasing: M E two M, two L and two N, for orders by material, supplier and number; M E eight zero F N for general analysis; M E five A for requisitions; and M E three L or three M for outline agreements. For inventory: M M B E for the stock overview, M B five two for warehouse stock, M B five one for material documents, M B five B for stock on a past date, M B five T for stock in transit, and M E two O for subcontracting stock. For invoices: M I R five for the invoice list, M B five S for G R I R balances, and M R B R for blocked invoices. In Fiori, look for the procurement overview page, with cards for spend, open orders and overdue items, and apps such as Monitor Purchase Order Items, Off-Contract Spend and Supplier Evaluation, plus Stock Multiple Materials and Inventory K P I Analysis. Names vary by release, so check your system. And for any classic report, teach the A L V tools: filter, sort, sum, subtotal, change the layout, save the layout, and export to a spreadsheet. Teaching end users to save their own layout is a five-minute win they'll thank you for.

lessons.title: S/4HANA simplifications in MM
lessons.body:
What changed from ECC: essential for trainers teaching migration projects.

AreaS/4HANA
SuppliersBusiness Partner mandatory; XK01 etc. redirect to BP
Material documentsSingle table MATDOC; no stock aggregate tables to update; faster
Goods movementsOld MB01/MB1A/MB1B/MB1C replaced by MIGO
Material numberUp to 40 characters
MRPMRP Live (MD01N) on HANA
ValuationMaterial ledger mandatory
AccountingUniversal Journal (table ACDOCA): FI and CO in one line item
UIFiori launchpad, role-based apps, overview pages
ApprovalsFlexible workflow alongside classic release strategies
OutputOutput Management (BRF+) alongside NAST

SAP publishes the full list in the Simplification List for each release.

Migration training sessions often start with “what changed for me?”. This table answers it.
lessons.narration: If you train on migration projects, users will always ask: what changed for me? Here's the answer for MM. Suppliers are now business partners, and the old vendor transactions redirect to B P. Material documents live in a single table, MATDOC, which makes stock reporting much faster. The old goods movement transactions, M B zero one and the M B one family, are replaced by M I G O. Material numbers can be up to forty characters. Planning uses M R P Live, running inside HANA. The material ledger is mandatory for valuation. Accounting uses the Universal Journal, table A C D O C A, where finance and controlling share one line item. The user interface is the Fiori launchpad, with role-based apps and overview pages. Approvals can use flexible workflow alongside classic release strategies. And output can use S/4HANA output management alongside the classic message framework. SAP publishes the complete list in the simplification list for each release. Keep this table handy: migration training sessions often open with exactly this question.
keyTerms: Single S/4HANA table for material documents
SAP's official list of changes per S/4HANA release
Old goods movement transactions replaced by MIGO

lessons.title: Preparing for C_TS452
lessons.body:
The assessment

  • SAP Certified – SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, Sourcing and Procurement (C_TS452)
  • System-based: you perform tasks in a real system, not just answer multiple-choice questions
  • About 3 hours; pass mark around 76% (check learning.sap.com for current details)
  • Booked via SAP Learning / Certification Hub; annual 'stay certified' assessment

Topic coverage (map to this course)

  • Enterprise structure → Module 1
  • Master data → Modules 2–3
  • Procurement processes → Modules 4–5
  • Inventory management → Module 6
  • Invoice verification & account determination → Module 7
  • Pricing, release, output → Module 8
  • MRP, special procurement, valuation → Module 9

Strategy

  1. Redo every 'Try it' task without notes
  2. Take every module quiz until you score 90%+
  3. Practise configuration paths in SPRO (read-only first)
  4. Use SAP's official learning journey and sample questions
  5. In the exam: do tasks you know first, flag the others, watch the clock

Always check the official exam page for the current topic areas and weightings before booking.
lessons.narration: The certification you're aiming for is SAP Certified, S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, Sourcing and Procurement, code C T S four five two. It's now system-based, which means you perform tasks in a real system rather than just answering multiple-choice questions. It lasts about three hours, the pass mark is around seventy-six percent, and you'll need to complete a stay-certified assessment each year. Always check learning dot sap dot com for the current details. The topics map neatly onto this course: enterprise structure in module one, master data in modules two and three, procurement processes in four and five, inventory in six, invoice verification and account determination in seven, pricing, release and output in eight, and planning, special procurement and valuation in nine. Here's a strategy. Redo every try-it task without notes. Take every module quiz until you score above ninety percent. Practise configuration paths in S P R O. Use SAP's official learning journey and sample questions. And in the exam itself, do the tasks you know first, flag the others, and watch the clock.
keyTerms: SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, Sourcing and Procurement certification

lessons.title: Packaging your sellable module
lessons.body:
Products you can sell

  • End-user training for companies migrating to S/4HANA: 1–3 days, role-based (buyer, warehouse, accounts payable)
  • Key-user training: 3–5 days, deeper, includes basic configuration awareness
  • Online self-study: this site, with accounts and payments added later

Training-centre requirements (France)

  • Clear objectives, programme, duration, prerequisites, assessment methods
  • Pre- and post-training assessment (module quizzes work well)
  • Attendance and completion evidence, satisfaction survey (Qualiopi indicators)

Your kit from this course

  • Org-structure diagram, navigation cheat sheet (M1)
  • Supplier creation job aid (M2), product master field guide (M3)
  • P2P demo scenario + workbook (M4), purchasing exercises (M5)
  • Movement-type card (M6), invoice-matching exercises (M7)
  • Approval demo (M8), MRP walkthrough (M9), 'What changed' handout (M10)

Start selling with the 1-day 'P2P in S/4HANA for end users'. It's the most in-demand format and uses Modules 1, 2 and 4.
lessons.narration: Let's finish by turning this course into something you can sell. There are three obvious products. First, end-user training for companies migrating to S/4HANA: one to three days, role-based, for buyers, warehouse staff or accounts payable. Second, key-user training: three to five days, deeper, with some configuration awareness. Third, online self-study, which is this site, with accounts and payments added later. If you sell through French training centres, you'll need clear objectives, a programme, duration, prerequisites and assessment methods; a pre- and post-training assessment, and the module quizzes work well for that; plus attendance evidence and a satisfaction survey, to meet Qualiopi requirements. And you've been building your kit all along: the org structure diagram and navigation cheat sheet, the supplier job aid, the product master field guide, the P2P demo and workbook, purchasing exercises, the movement type card, invoice matching exercises, the approval demo, the M R P walkthrough, and the what changed handout. My advice: start selling with a one-day course, P2P in S/4HANA for end users. It's the most in-demand format, and it uses modules one, two and four.
keyTerms: Role-based, process-focused training for daily users
Deeper training for super-users who support colleagues
